payload.instruction: Change the background into a basketball court
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Has the image background been changed into a recognizable basketball court?
node.criteria: The edited background visibly depicts a basketball court, identifiable from the background as a playing area with court context or markings, or from basketball equipment integrated into a visible playing surface. A sparse or stylized court can fully satisfy the endpoint when the background as a whole is clearly recognizable as a basketball court; basketball-related objects against an otherwise ambiguous background alone are not enough.
node.binding: Compare SOURCE and EDITED: determine whether the background in EDITED is a recognizable basketball court rather than the original background. Judge the background as a whole; do not require broad court context or a particular number of markings when visible court features make its identity clear.
node.source_quote: Change the background into a basketball court
node.endpoint: The background is visibly recognizable as a basketball court.
node.necessity: Changing the background into a basketball court is the explicit requested edit.
node.zero_when: The background shows no requested change toward depicting a basketball court; unrelated edits do not count.
node.half_when: The background has concrete basketball-court cues, but the background as a whole remains genuinely ambiguous or incomplete as a playing court—for example, basketball equipment appears without enough visible playing-surface or court context to establish the setting.
node.full_when: The background as a whole is clearly recognizable as a basketball court from visible court context, markings, or basketball equipment integrated with a playing surface. Sparse or stylized context is acceptable when the court identity is clear; natural variation in lighting, texture, or photographic appearance is acceptable.
